user_action_gates.message: The first end-to-end long-form pipeline is ready for real-world validation. Stop development-only work and start producing real videos: only real recordings can show whether the editing is good, and the finished long-form videos become the source material for Phase 7 short-form repurposing. This is readiness to begin validation, not proof that production-quality editing has been achieved.
steps: Tell Lukas, in plain words, that the pipeline is ready for real-world validation and that development-only work should pause.
Give him the filming checklist in AI_Creator_Studio_Documentation/FIRST_REAL_VIDEO_CHECKLIST.md and explain which footage, audio and recording variety are useful.
Explain how to ingest the footage safely: place it under Incoming/<project-name>/, catalogue it in place, never move or edit originals, keep a separate backup, and run inspection before ingestion.

With Lukas's permission, start validating long-form editing against the real recordings; record every real run and its human review as evidence in PROJECT_STATUS.json (a milestone counts as verified only after he has reviewed the result).
Plan Phase 7 short-form repurposing on the long-form videos produced this way.
Set this gate to ACKNOWLEDGED (acknowledged_by, acknowledged_date) only after Lukas confirms he has read it.
user_action_gates.notification: In the repository, `governance validate` (it fails once the trigger fires while the gate is PENDING) and the generated SESSION_HANDOFF.md are the reminders. REPORTED by Lukas, not verified by Claude: a weekly ChatGPT automation named "Phase 6 Readiness Check" is scheduled inside ChatGPT. NOT VERIFIED: that this automation can read the private repository or has completed any check; no completed run is recorded here. The automation does not trigger, replace or acknowledge the gate; only milestone evidence and validation trigger it and only Lukas acknowledges it.

readiness_criteria.text: Source footage is processed through the editing pipeline (ingest, understanding, plan) by the pipeline itself.
A validated edit plan is produced and a Resolve timeline is built from it.
A complete long-form output is rendered.
Initial automated QC and export verification are completed on that output.
Originals are preserved (verified unchanged) and the project state stays recoverable throughout.

checklist_summary: Pick a real topic you would publish anyway; plan one or two long-form videos of roughly 8 to 20 minutes.
Do a 30-second audio test first; use your best microphone at a steady distance; record 20 to 30 seconds of room tone.
Use a constant frame rate where possible (variable frame rate is refused by shot detection, Q22).
Record variety: calm and animated passages, a joke, a restart or repeated phrase, quiet and fast speech, a second angle or phone clip, screen recording and short B-roll if relevant.
Keep your notes on what must not be cut (names, jokes, claims). Avoid music or footage you have no rights to.
Put the files in Incoming/<project-name>/ yourself and keep a second backup copy on another drive before anything touches them.
Ask for incoming-list and incoming-inspect (dry runs) first; ingest only after you agree; originals are never moved, edited or deleted.
Your review of each result is what makes a milestone verified; it is recorded as evidence.
